display.purpose: Hero headlines, service names in commitment cards, sidebar logo, currency amounts in feature cards. Never in operational UI.

body.purpose: All operational UI text: navigation, buttons, form labels, descriptions, card titles. Maximum 65ch for prose.

label.purpose: Status badges, codes, identifiers, timestamps, table column headers, financial metadata. Always uppercase at smallest sizes.

shadows.name: whisper
shadows.purpose: Resting state of interactive controls (buttons, chips). Signals affordance without distraction.

shadows.name: structural
shadows.purpose: Hover state on controls, dropdowns at rest, focus panels.

shadows.name: card-deep
shadows.purpose: Commitment cards — floating physical card metaphor only.

motion.name: standard
motion.purpose: Default for state transitions: color, background, shadow, opacity.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Sidebar visibility threshold. Below md: sidebar hidden.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Dashboard grid shifts from 1 to 2 columns.

narrative.overview:
Aliran is a shared household finance tracker used by families who want a single, honest view of where money flows. The design system takes its metaphor from a well-kept physical ledger: authoritative but domestic, precise without being cold. Every surface serves the record. Every element earns its place on the page.

The aesthetic is light, warm, and fixed — a deliberate choice made for a couple at the kitchen table, laptop open, reviewing what's due this month. The cream-parchment background is the paper. The forest green is the ink of authority. The serif display face appears only where the record needs a name and falls away entirely for the operational UI that surrounds it.

Aliran explicitly rejects: the widget-heavy dashboard congestion of Mint and YNAB; the dark-mode hype of trading and crypto apps; and the generic SaaS layout language of sidebar-plus-identical-card-grids.
keyCharacteristics: Warm parchment light surface, forest green as the single authority accent
Three-font system with strict role separation: display (serif), sans (Inter), mono (JetBrains)
Full-palette semantic color for financial categories — sealed to data meaning, never decoration
Tonal layering for content; structural shadow for interactive controls
Tabular numerals throughout all monetary values

rules.name: The Semantic Seal Rule
rules.body: The four finance-category colors (income/expense/scheduled/receivable) are sealed to their semantic roles. No other element in the UI uses these colors.

rules.name: The OKLCH Doctrine
rules.body: All color tokens are defined in OKLCH. The project does not use hex as a source-of-truth. Accept Stitch linter warnings.

rules.name: The Instrument Rule
rules.body: Instrument Serif appears for: service names, currency amounts, the sidebar logo, and hero headlines only. It is prohibited in buttons, form labels, navigation, table headers, and status indicators.

rules.name: The Tabular Number Rule
rules.body: All monetary values must carry font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums and font-feature-settings: tnum. Amounts in tables must align on the decimal point.

rules.name: The Flat Content Rule
rules.body: Cards, data tables, section containers, and dashboard tiles are flat at rest. Shadow on a card makes it feel like a button.

dos: Do use Instrument Serif for service names, currency amounts, the sidebar logo, and hero headlines only.
Do apply JetBrains Mono to all codes, identifiers, timestamps, table column headers, and status labels.
Do apply font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums to every monetary value.
Do use the four semantic colors (income/expense/scheduled/receivable) exclusively for their financial category.
Do keep content surfaces flat: cream-50 cards on cream-100 ground, ring hairline outline only.
Do render negative numbers, zero balances, and overdue commitments clearly and without alarm.
Do vary spacing for rhythm: 8px, 12px, 16px, 24px are different notes.
Do use the --line token for all borders and dividers.
donts: Don't create widget-heavy layouts in the style of Mint or YNAB.
Don't use dark-mode hype aesthetics: neon accents, gamified UI, animated score counters.
Don't default to generic SaaS layout: sidebar plus identical card grids.
Don't use side-stripe borders (border-left or border-right greater than 1px as colored accent).
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient fill).
Don't use the four semantic category colors for hover states, focus rings, or decorative accents.
Don't add shadow to flat content cards.
Don't use Instrument Serif in buttons, form labels, navigation, table headers, or status indicators.
Don't animate layout properties (width, height, padding, margin).
Don't use #000 or #fff — every neutral is tinted toward the brand hue.
